sources.citation: Sourati, Zhivar, et al. (2026). The shrinking landscape of linguistic diversity in the age of large language models. Nature Human Behaviour.
sources.study_domain: Seven datasets spanning Reddit WritingPrompts, arXiv abstracts, local news, congressional speech, social posts, questionnaires, and empathic conversations; more than 880,000 texts.
sources.measured: LLM polishing/rewriting retained core content while reducing writing-complexity variance by 21-50% across the reported datasets and models.
sources.limitations: The reported datasets, models, prompts, and complexity measures do not establish that any individual text is AI-written, that every rewrite is harmful, or a universal preferred writing style.
sources.supports_operational_rule: No direct rule; supports a contextual preserve-first review for meaningful personal or cultural variation.

sources.citation: Miletic, Filip and Neele Falk (2026). What Are LLMs Doing to Scientific Communication? Measuring Changes in Writing Practices and Reading Experience. LREC 2026, pp. 1811-1830.
sources.study_domain: Natural-language-processing scholarly communication: a corpus of more than 37,000 ACL Anthology papers (2020-2024), 3,000 human passages with LLM improvements, and a pilot of 20 domain experts.
sources.measured: The authors report diachronic lexical changes; LLM-modified passages more often had specified syntactic constructions, longer and more complex words, and lower lexical diversity. The 20-expert pilot reported both higher understandability/excitement and negative qualitative attitudes.
sources.limitations: This is NLP scholarly prose with a small subjective-reading pilot. It neither ranks general-purpose prose quality nor establishes that a named construction is intrinsically bad.
sources.supports_operational_rule: No direct rule; supports checking repeated patterns in context and retaining clarity where a change improves reading experience.

sources.citation: Agarwal, Dhruv, Mor Naaman, and Aditya Vashistha (2025). AI Suggestions Homogenize Writing Toward Western Styles and Diminish Cultural Nuances. CHI 2025, article 1117.
sources.study_domain: Controlled English-language, culturally grounded writing tasks completed by 118 participants in India and the United States with and without GPT-4o autocomplete suggestions.
sources.measured: The study reports higher efficiency gains for American participants and increased convergence of Indian writing toward American styles under the studied suggestions, including changes in cultural nuance.
sources.limitations: The result concerns one model, autocomplete interaction, two participant groups, English tasks, and the study design. It does not license a generic classifier for culture or a universal rule about directness, formality, or lexical diversity.
sources.supports_operational_rule: No direct rule; supports preserving user-supplied cultural and personal choices unless a concrete audience or factual need justifies change.

sources.citation: Kobak, Dmitry, Rita Gonzalez-Marquez, Emoke-Agnes Horvat, and Jan Lause (2025). Delving into LLM-assisted writing in biomedical publications through excess vocabulary. Science Advances 11(27), eadt3813.
sources.study_domain: More than 15 million English-language PubMed biomedical abstracts from 2010-2024, analysed at corpus level.
sources.measured: The authors measured abrupt post-ChatGPT frequency increases in hundreds of style-affecting words and estimate a lower bound for LLM processing in 2024 biomedical abstracts using excess vocabulary.
sources.limitations: Corpus-level excess vocabulary cannot identify individual abstracts, prove authorship, evaluate all prose, or make any word universally undesirable. The record is biomedical abstracts, not general writing.
sources.supports_operational_rule: No direct rule; supports treating clusters and local repetition as candidates for review rather than word bans or authorship conclusions.

sources.citation: Weber-Wulff, Debora, et al. (2023). Testing of detection tools for AI-generated text. International Journal for Educational Integrity 19, 26.
sources.study_domain: Academic-context audit of 12 public and two commercial detection tools using an original document set, including translation and obfuscation conditions.
sources.measured: The authors evaluated detector accuracy and error types and concluded that the tested tools were neither accurate nor reliable under their conditions; obfuscation worsened performance.
sources.limitations: The 2023 tool set and test materials do not prove every later detector has identical performance. The study does not justify evasion, nor does it validate individual authorship claims.
sources.supports_operational_rule: Direct boundary: abstain from detector scores, authorship conclusions, and detector-evasion advice; offer legitimate clarity or style help instead.
